stem:
Two progressive waves meet at a point.
Which condition must be met for superposition of the waves to occur?

options.B: The waves must be of the same type.
options.C: The waves must be travelling in opposite directions.
options.D: The waves must meet in phase.

stem:
The principle of superposition states that a certain quantity is added when two or more waves
meet at a point.
What is this quantity?

Two waves of the same type overlap.
When does the principle of superposition apply?

options.B: only when the waves have the same amplitude
options.C: only when the waves have the same frequency
options.D: only when the waves travel in opposite directions

stem: What happens when two waves superpose at a point?
Which statement concerning a stationary wave is correct?

options.A: All the particles between two adjacent nodes oscillate in phase.
options.B: The amplitude of the stationary wave is equal to the amplitude of one of the waves creating it.
options.C: The wavelength of the stationary wave is equal to the separation of two adjacent nodes.
options.D: There is no displacement of a particle at an antinode at any time.

stem:
Two progressive sound waves move in opposite directions and superpose to form a stationary
wave.
Which statement describes an antinode of this stationary wave?

options.A: a position where the phase difference between the two waves is always 0°
options.B: a position where the phase difference between the two waves is always 180°
options.C: a position where the stationary wave has maximum amplitude
options.D: a position where the stationary wave has minimum amplitude

stem:
Two progressive waves overlap.
What is an essential condition for the two waves to form a stationary wave?

options.C: The waves travel in opposite directions.
options.D: The waves travel in the same direction.

distributed along the length of a horizontal glass tube which is closed at one end.
At the open end of the tube, a loudspeaker emits a sound wave of a constant wavelength. A
stationary wave is formed and the powder accumulates in regularly spaced piles, as shown.

options.B: The piles are where the air molecules vibrate with minimum amplitude.
options.C: The piles are where the air molecules vibrate with the highest frequency.
options.D: The piles are where the air molecules vibrate vertically.

Which distance is equal to the wavelength of the wave?

options.A: double the distance between adjacent antinodes
options.B: half the distance between adjacent nodes
options.D: the distance between a node and an adjacent antinode
